So the functionality here is just server based speech to text and showing that on the screen in the PWA.
Does the PWA allow for functioning in the background?
You're correct - the MVP I outlined is just server-based STT displayed in the PWA.
And you've hit on a critical limitation: PWAs have significant restrictions on background functionality, especially for continuous audio recording.

## PWA Background Limitations
Continuous audio recording (browsers suspend MediaStream when backgrounded)
WebRTC connections (typically disconnected when tab loses focus)
WebSocket connections (throttled or closed after ~30 seconds)
JavaScript execution (heavily throttled or paused)
Service Workers can run briefly for specific events
Push notifications can wake the app
Background sync for queued data upload
Limited background fetch (periodic, not continuous)



Your extended cognition concept requires always-on listening, which PWAs simply cannot deliver.
When the user switches apps or locks their phone, audio capture stops.

## Alternative Approaches
PWA for active conversations (tab in foreground)
Native companion app for background recording
Sync between them via shared backend
PWA stays dormant
User says "Hey Claude" to activate
Similar to Alexa/Siri model
Keep tablet/phone with PWA always open
Screen stays on, app in foreground
Works for desk/home scenarios














Given your September 2025 timeline, I suggest:
Start with Foreground-Only PWA (Week 1-4)
Proves the pipeline works
Tests latency and performance
No platform-specific complexity
Add Electron Wrapper (Week 5-8)
Enables true background recording on desktop
Minimal code changes from PWA
Good for demos and personal use
Consider Mobile Native (Post-demo)
React Native or Flutter
For real extended cognition use

So again this is not media stream we're not storing anything on the device but webrtc connections being disconnected so if I if I'm pull up this app and start a stream and I press the power button to conserve power will this stop?

I think I also wanna focus on the PWA around its capability of wake words like I I wanna I wanna identify it's potential for running in the background that is running while the user is not focused on it because I don't want them to have to look at the screen I want them to be able to put this in their pocket and forget about it wearing a lapel mic so they pick somebody clearly but so the two things I'm concerned about are can it continue the webrtc stream when the screen is locked in the background and can't it be activated by wake word?
You're asking the right questions for your vision.

Let me be direct about PWA capabilities for your use case:



Short answer: No, WebRTC streams stop when the screen is locked or app is backgrounded.

iOS Safari: Aggressively suspends everything (WebRTC dies in ~5 seconds)
Chrome Android: Slightly more lenient but still kills streams (~30 seconds)
Desktop browsers: Keep connections alive longer when minimized, not indefinitely



Also no - PWAs cannot listen for wake words in the background.

Wake word detection requires:
Continuous audio processing
Running while app isn't active
Ability to "wake up" the app

PWAs have none of these capabilities.
The browser won't let you keep recording audio when the user isn't actively using your app.

## Your Pocket + Lapel Mic Vision

This is exactly what PWAs cannot do.

The moment users put the phone in their pocket:
Screen locks → WebRTC stops
App backgrounds → No audio access
No wake word detection possible
Raspberry Pi with mic running your software
Always-on Android device with custom app
Smart glasses/earbuds with built-in processing
Native app for continuous recording
PWA for rich UI when actively using
Same backend infrastructure



Since PWA won't work for background recording, consider:
Accept PWA Limitations: Build your MVP as "active use only" - great for desktop/tablet scenarios where screen stays on
Plan for Native: Your true vision requires React Native or Flutter.
The WebRTC/streaming code you write now will port over.

Test the Pipeline First: Even with foreground-only PWA, you can validate:
Streaming architecture works
STT latency is acceptable  
Backend can handle continuous audio

Would you like me to:
Show you a React Native setup that actually supports background audio?
- Modify the MVP to work within PWA constraints?
- Explore dedicated hardware options?
Your pocket + lapel mic vision is totally achievable - just not with a PWA.

You're onto something important!
Yes, you can potentially leverage the system's built-in wake word detection rather than building your own.

## System Wake Word Integration
iOS: Limited to Siri Shortcuts (can't use custom wake words)
Android: More flexible with Assistant integration
Neither: Allows continuous background listening with custom wake words





Vision: Put your phone in your pocket with a lapel mic and let Extended Cognition become your invisible AI companion - capturing, understanding, organizing your entire day without any interaction.

### Core Features:
Continuous audio streaming while phone is locked
Works with screen off to save battery
Processes everything from meetings to random thoughts
No need to press any buttons or look at screen
System wake word: "Hey Siri/OK Google, activate Extended Cognition"
Vibration confirmation when recording starts/stops
Optional periodic pulse to confirm it's still listening
Real-time transcription and understanding
Automatic extraction of tasks, ideas, commitments
Context-aware note creation
Meeting summaries generated automatically
All processing happens on your local hardware
Audio archived only on your personal server
Face ID/fingerprint protection for access
Automatic pause in bathrooms/private spaces (GPS-based)

Feature: Stream audio in background, PWA: ❌, Native App: ✅.
Feature: Wake word activation, PWA: ❌, Native App: ✅ (via Siri/Google).
Feature: 8+ hour continuous recording, PWA: ❌, Native App: ✅.

Feature: Battery optimization, PWA: ❌, Native App: ✅ Background modes.

Extended cognition isn't one of them.
Your vision of putting a phone in your pocket and having it act as an intelligent audio companion is 100% achievable - but only with native development.
The good news: your backend architecture (STT, LLM, knowledge storage) remains exactly the same.
